clue.text: Party set at sixes and sevens — that's material

indicators.note: a phrase meaning in total disorder, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A party in complete disarray turns out to be the stuff of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sixes and sevens' rearranges PARTY SET into the woven fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a heavy woven fabric with a pictorial design, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: A winger requiring medical treatment

definitions.meaning: a bird, something with wings, here a songbird
a fungal infection that needs a doctor's care

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing needs to see the physio.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a common songbird and a yeast infection that has to be treated.

clue.text: Step over to check the pie

parts.note: a pas is a step in dance, from the French
to try a thing is to test or check it

explanation.surface: Someone walks over to inspect the pie on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: PAS is the ballet word for a step; 'over to' merely joins it to the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is the baked dough that makes the crust of a pie, and the word also covers pies and tarts as a group.

clue.text: as she lacks pie for hampers

indicators.note: printer's pie is type spilt into a jumble, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: She has no pie to put in the picnic baskets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' is the printers' word for jumbled type, so it rearranges SHE LACKS; 'hampers' is a verb, not the baskets the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Shackles restrain and restrict movement, just as something that hampers holds one back.

clue.text: Appear unstable though a dependable sort

definitions.meaning: to sway to and fro as if about to fall
a person others can lean on, steady as stone

explanation.surface: Someone seems shaky yet is reliable all the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway back and forth looks unsteady, while a person who is a tower of strength is called by the same word for solid stone.

clue.text: Subordinate taking a sly glance around the ship

indicators.note: the glance goes round the outside of the vessel, enclosing it

parts.note: a leer is a sly or knowing look
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A junior officer eyes the vessel with a sly look.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lesser is lower in rank or importance, which is what subordinate means.

clue.text: A hellish place before public transport

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Somewhere awful comes just before you catch the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Erebus is the dark region of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Erebus was the gloomy underworld of Greek mythology, a place of the dead through which souls passed to Hades.

clue.text: Tops up credit arrangements — wide-ranging

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Tops up credit arrangements — wide-ranging (8)', has no fodder giving SPACIOUS (no T in the answer, and no A, I or second S in the clue's short words); the clue looks misread in OCR and no source gives the printed text.

clue.text: Shy about dressing

parts.note: re means about or concerning
tiring is an old word for dressing or attiring, as in tiring-room

explanation.surface: Someone is bashful when it comes to getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRING is the old word for attiring, kept in 'tiring-house', the actors' dressing room.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person tends to avoid company and attention, which is what being shy means.

clue.text: Look, not for the first time, for scientific investigation

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, so something done once more
to search is to look for something

explanation.surface: A scientist looks again and again in the name of investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as RE-SEARCH, the answer is literally to look again.
explanation.definitionFit: Research is systematic study carried out to establish facts, as in a laboratory investigation.

clue.text: Fussy academic's huff about a newspaper leader

indicators.note: the breathing word goes round the outside of the editor, enclosing it

parts.note: to huff is to puff or pant
ED is short for editor, the person in charge of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A fussy don is in a sulk about a newspaper editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huff' looks like a sulk, but it is the puffing sense; 'leader' is not an editorial article but the person leading the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone obsessively concerned with minor details and rules, especially in learning.

clue.text: The board holds a couple of points to be reasonable

indicators.note: the board keeps the points inside it, containing them

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board
E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: The committee's board agrees two items, which seems fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable argument can be defended, so it is reasonable and sound.

clue.text: Attack a rowing man

definitions.meaning: a sudden seizure, as of apoplexy
the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the rhythm

explanation.surface: An oarsman suddenly goes on the offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden fit such as a brain seizure and the oarsman who sets the pace in a racing eight.

clue.text: Unconventional individual

definitions.meaning: belonging to one person or thing alone

explanation.surface: Describing an eccentric loner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means odd or strange and also particular to one person, as in a custom peculiar to a region.

clue.text: Putting fifty thousand into these components can provide capital protection

indicators.note: the two Roman numerals are put inside the rearranged word
the parts of the word are taken apart and reassembled

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Investing fifty thousand in these parts could keep your capital safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'components' rearranges THESE as HEETS, and 'into' puts LM inside; 'capital' is the head, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmets protect the head, and capital comes from the Latin for head.

clue.text: Few will be cut by a pound

parts.note: to sever is to cut
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A small number will be cut back by a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means more than two but not many, which is close to a few.

clue.text: Hurriedly withdraw holding unit in defeat

indicators.note: the retreating word keeps the figure inside it, containing it

parts.note: to run is to flee in a hurry
I is the Roman numeral for one, a unit

explanation.surface: Troops beat a hasty retreat, a unit among them, in defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is total downfall or overthrow, the state that defeat brings about.

clue.text: Offering to serve the people

parts.note: to do is to serve or suffice, as in that will do
a nation is a people united by country

explanation.surface: Something given in order to serve the community.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, something offered freely to a cause.

clue.text: Do not consider a mark-down

explanation.surface: Ignore the sale price.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to dismiss from consideration and also a cut in the price of goods.

clue.text: Fabulous animal carrying scholar and guide

indicators.note: the beast holds the graduate inside it, bearing it

parts.note: a dragon is a creature of fable
MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar

explanation.surface: A mythical beast bears a learned man and his guide.
explanation.walkthrough: A dragoman was an interpreter and guide in Arabic, Turkish or Persian-speaking lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an interpreter who also acted as guide to travellers in the Middle East.

clue.text: Love-bird painter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: An artist who paints lovebirds.
explanation.walkthrough: John Opie was an 18th-century Cornish portrait painter; 'Love-bird' looks like one creature but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: John Opie was a Cornish portraitist and history painter of the late 1700s.

clue.text: A young rascal learning to beg

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lore is knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A naughty child learning to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead earnestly, which is to beg.

clue.text: A writer's alternative correctly used

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
done well is done properly or correctly

explanation.surface: An author's choice of words used rightly.
explanation.walkthrough: George Orwell wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four and Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the English novelist and essayist behind Animal Farm.

clue.text: Speak of popular heavyweight. English

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: Talk about a well-liked heavyweight who is English.
explanation.definitionFit: To intone is to speak or recite in a measured, chanting voice.

clue.text: Dormant talent should be developed

indicators.note: developing changes the form, so the letters of the word are reworked

explanation.surface: A hidden gift ought to be nurtured.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent is present but not yet active or visible, much as something dormant is asleep.

clue.text: Bill the junior minister is quite right

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant to a parish priest, a junior clergyman

explanation.surface: The bill presented by the junior politician is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junior minister' looks political but means a church minister: a curate assists the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means precise and correct, exactly right.

clue.text: Grow old and maybe find various things needing attention

parts.note: to age is to grow old

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word could be put another way, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: As you get older you find a list of jobs to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the signal to rearrange the little linking-looking word that follows the first piece; 'find' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, as at a meeting.

clue.text: A man in clerical attire

indicators.note: the name sits inside the word clerical, dressed in it

explanation.surface: A fellow dressed in a priest's garb.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a man's first name.

clue.text: In running water many get hardened

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
D is the Roman numeral for 500, many

explanation.surface: Many in the cold river become toughened.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river; D (500) stands for 'many' by convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inured has become accustomed to hardship, toughened against it.

clue.text: Plain words about the border — a sign Spring has come!

indicators.note: the plain words go round the outside of the edge, enclosing it

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing, not verse
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Simple language around the flowerbed edge heralds the arrival of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' looks like a garden bed, fitting the scene, but just means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is one of the earliest wild flowers of the year, a classic herald of the new season.

clue.text: Clear of all charges and let out to cause bother

parts.note: a net sum is what remains after deductions

indicators.note: out suggests the word is put out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is cleared of the charges and released, only to stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the signal to rearrange the short word; 'Clear of all charges' looks legal but is the financial sense of a sum after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle is to irritate or annoy, the way a stinging plant does.

clue.text: The least adequate look closely at the criterion

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely
a test is a standard or criterion

explanation.surface: The poorest examine the benchmark closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, so the scantest is the least sufficient.
